st: Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt, [[0.5 tsp]] black pepper and [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric. Rub well and let sit 10 minutes.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a wide heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken skin side down for 5 minutes, flip, and brown 3 more minutes, then set aside.
Lower the heat to medium and add the grated onions. Cook 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic and [[1 tbsp]] grated ginger for 1 minute. Add the saffron with its water and [[1 cup]] water.
Return the chicken to the pot, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook on low for 40 minutes.
Add the sliced preserved lemon rind and [[0.5 cup]] olives. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the sauce is thick and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] chopped cilantro and serve with crusty bread.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a large pot. Brown the lamb for 8 minutes with the sliced onion.
Add [[1 tsp]] ginger, [[1 tsp]] turmeric, [[1 tsp]] black pepper, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the saffron. Pour in [[8 cups]] water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 1 hour until the lamb is almost tender.
Add the carrots, turnips, quartered onion and chickpeas. Simmer 15 minutes.
Add the squash and zucchini and simmer 15 more minutes until everything is tender. Stir in the cilantro.
Meanwhile, put [[3 cups]] couscous in a wide bowl. Dissolve [[1 tsp]] salt in [[3 cups]] warm water and sprinkle over, stirring with a fork. Let it swell 10 minutes.
Break up the clumps with your fingers, dot with [[3 tbsp]] butter, and fluff. Cover to keep warm.
Pile the couscous on a big platter, arrange the meat and vegetables on top, and ladle broth over. Serve extra broth in a bowl.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a large pot. Brown the lamb cubes with the grated onion and celery for 8 minutes.
Stir in [[1 tsp]] ginger, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric, [[0.5 tsp]] cinnamon and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper, then the grated tomatoes and [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste. Cook 5 minutes.
Add [[6 cups]] water, the rinsed lentils and [[2 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer 35 minutes.
Add the chickpeas, [[0.5 cup]] cilantro and [[0.5 cup]] parsley. Simmer 10 minutes.
Whisk [[3 tbsp]] flour with [[1 cup]] cold water until smooth, then pour it slowly into the pot while stirring.
Add the vermicelli and simmer 10 minutes, stirring often, until the soup thickens and the noodles are soft.
Taste for salt and serve hot with lemon wedges and dates if you like.
Put the chicken, onions, [[4 tbsp]] butter, [[1 tsp]] ginger, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric, saffron, pepper, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[1.5 cups]] water in a pot. Cover and simmer 45 minutes.
Lift the chicken out, cool, then shred the meat and discard skin and bones. Boil the sauce uncovered 10 minutes until about [[1 cup]] remains.
Lower the heat, add [[2 tbsp]] lemon juice and the beaten eggs, and stir gently until just set into soft curds, about 3 minutes. Mix in the shredded chicken and parsley. Cool completely.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan 4 minutes, then chop coarsely and mix with [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] cinnamon.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Melt the remaining butter. Brush a 10 inch round pan with butter and layer 5 phyllo sheets, overlapping and hanging over the sides, brushing each.
Spread half the almond mix, then all the chicken mix, then the rest of the almonds. Fold the overhang over the top.
Cover with the remaining sheets, brushed with butter, and tuck the edges under. Bake 30 minutes until deep golden.
Dust with [[2 tbsp]] powdered sugar, then make a pattern with [[1 tsp]] cinnamon and [[2 tbsp]] sugar. Rest 10 minutes and slice.
In a bowl, mix the beef, grated onion, half the garlic, parsley, cilantro, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] paprika, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper until sticky. Shape into walnut-size balls.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the sliced onion for 5 minutes, then add the remaining garlic for 1 minute.
Add the grated tomatoes, [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] paprika, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 cup]] water. Simmer 10 minutes.
Nestle the meatballs into the sauce, cover, and cook on low for 15 minutes, turning once, until they reach 160°F (71°C).
Make 4 small wells between the meatballs and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook 5 to 7 minutes until the whites are set but yolks are still soft. Serve in the pan with bread.
Toss the lamb with [[1 tsp]] ginger, [[1 tsp]] cinnamon, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric, saffron, pepper and [[1.5 tsp]] salt. Let sit 15 minutes.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a Dutch oven and brown the lamb in batches, 6 minutes per batch.
Add the sliced onions and the cinnamon stick and cook 5 minutes.
Pour in [[2 cups]] water, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low for 1 hour 15 minutes until the lamb is very tender.
Add the prunes and [[3 tbsp]] honey. Simmer uncovered 15 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan 4 minutes until golden.
Spoon the lamb onto a platter, sprinkle with almonds and [[1 tbsp]] sesame seeds. Serve with bread or couscous.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Prick the eggplants all over with a fork and roast on a tray for 40 minutes until collapsed and soft.
Cool a few minutes, then scoop out the flesh and chop it. Discard the skin.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the grated tomatoes, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] paprika, cayenne and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Simmer the tomatoes for 10 minutes until thick and most of the liquid is gone.
Add the eggplant and mash with a spoon. Cook 10 minutes, stirring often, until it becomes a thick, chunky spread.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] olive oil, [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice and [[0.25 cup]] cilantro. Serve warm or cool with bread.
Wash the cilantro and parsley and dry them well. Chop them roughly.
Peel the garlic and crush it with [[1 tsp]] salt into a rough paste.
Put the herbs and garlic paste in a food processor, or chop finely by hand and mix in a bowl.
Add [[2 tsp]] cumin, [[2 tsp]] paprika, cayenne and the saffron if using.
Pour in [[0.25 cup]] lemon juice and [[0.5 cup]] olive oil, then pulse or stir until a loose, chunky sauce forms.
Taste and adjust salt or lemon. Rub it on fish and marinate 30 minutes before cooking, or spoon over cooked fish.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[1 cup]] semolina, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] sugar in a large bowl. Add about [[1.5 cups]] warm water and knead 10 minutes into a smooth, soft dough.
Divide into 12 balls, coat them lightly in oil, and rest covered for 20 minutes.
Mix the oil and [[4 tbsp]] melted butter in a small bowl. Oil your work surface.
Flatten a ball into a very thin, almost see-through square, using oiled hands and fingertips.
Brush the square with the oil-butter mix and sprinkle with semolina. Fold the four sides into the center like an envelope to make a small square.
Gently stretch the square to about 5 inches wide. Repeat with all balls, resting them covered.
Heat a dry skillet over medium heat. Cook each square 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and flaky.
Serve warm with honey, butter or jam.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[1 cup]] semolina, [[2 tsp]] yeast, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] sugar in a large bowl.
Add [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and about [[1.5 cups]] warm water. Stir until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead on a floured surface for 10 minutes until smooth and springy.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide in two and shape each into a tight round about 1 inch thick. Dust a tray with semolina and place the loaves on it.
Cover with a towel and let rise 40 minutes until puffy.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Prick each loaf a few times with a fork.
Bake 20 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped. Cool on a rack.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[0.25 cup]] toasted sesame seeds, [[1 tsp]] anise, [[1 tsp]] cinnamon, [[1 tsp]] yeast and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Add [[4 tbsp]] melted butter, the egg, [[2 tbsp]] orange blossom water and [[1 tbsp]] vinegar. Add warm water to make a soft dough, up to [[0.5 cup]].
Knead 8 minutes, cover, and rest 30 minutes.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into rectangles about 3 by 4 inches. Make 4 parallel slits in each, leaving the edges attached.
Weave your finger through alternate strips and fold to form a rose shape. Repeat with all dough.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil to 340°F (170°C). Fry the cookies in batches for 3 minutes until deep golden, then drain.
Warm [[1.5 cups]] honey with [[0.25 cup]] water in a wide pan over low heat for 3 minutes.
Dip the warm cookies in honey for 1 minute each, sprinkle with [[0.25 cup]] sesame seeds, and cool on a rack. They firm up as they sit.
Bring [[3.5 cups]] of water to a full boil in a kettle.
Put [[1 tbsp]] green tea in a teapot and pour in [[0.5 cup]] boiling water. Swirl for 30 seconds and pour off the liquid to rinse the leaves.
Add the mint, optional sage and [[0.25 cup]] sugar to the pot.
Pour the remaining [[3 cups]] boiling water over everything.
Steep for 5 minutes, then stir gently.
Pour a glass and return it to the pot two or three times to mix. Pour from a height into small glasses and serve hot.
